reconcile.note: Gill reads the twelve as the apostles' retained title, even though Judas's death left eleven and Thomas's absence left only ten present.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes that Acts has the Eleven filling Judas's vacancy while Paul still speaks of an appearance to "the twelve".

quotes.text: not only does the author of the Acts represent the twelve as so compact a body immediately after the ascension of their master, that they think it incumbent on them to fill up the breach made by the apostasy of Judas by the election of a new member…but the Apostle Paul also notices an appearance of the risen Jesus, specially to the twelve ( 1 Cor. xv. 5 ).
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §73, on 1 Corinthians 15:5.

sides.snippet: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn't with them when Jesus came.
